question: Should cron auto-delivery ever discard a plain-text payload based on an inferred prose pattern, or must suppression be represented by structured delivery/control state?
rationale: The intended regression is real, but accepting false-positive message loss versus adding a structured suppression contract is a product and delivery-semantics choice rather than a mechanical test fix.

options.title: Use structured suppression
options.body: Keep the prompt guidance and add or reuse a typed delivery/control signal so only explicitly non-deliverable output is suppressed.

options.title: Keep the lexical guard
options.body: Accept that some valid one-line recipient-led messages may be dropped, then document that tradeoff and add representative boundary coverage.

recommendation.title: Use structured suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the prompt guidance and add or reuse a typed delivery/control signal so only explicitly non-deliverable output is suppressed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history makes steipete the strongest routing candidate for cron direct-delivery semantics.
